circle_level_observations.text: Q7 explicitly names FOUR important non-family contacts — Ray Mendoza, Pastor Dale Hutchins, Walt Pearson, and Marcus — but the circle includes only Ray and Marcus. Pastor Dale Hutchins is referenced 6+ times across the interview (Q7, Q24, Q30, Q43, Q45, Q47, Q50) as Michael's pastor, historical-society board peer, post-father's-death counseling referrer, and 3-AM-worry confidant — arguably the strongest non-family confidant after Ray. He is a notable omission.

Walt Pearson (Q7, Q18) — community-center walking-club organizer Michael sees three mornings a week and who phones him when he misses a session — is also absent from the circle. Walt represents the daily-routine accountability tier of Michael's social fabric.

Brother Doug (Vancouver, WA, Q5/Q13) and Susan's sister Karen (Salem, Q6) are mentioned as extended-family contacts but are explicitly characterized as not close ('we see him on holidays', 'I get along with her fine, but we're not close'). Their absence from a tight five-person circle is consistent with the interview.

The mother Marjorie (Q35, Q44) is highly emotionally salient and visited weekly, but her advanced dementia means she is not a two-way text-message contact, so her absence from this five-member text-circle representation is structurally appropriate.

The five-member structural cap is preserved with two adult children (high-frequency text channels), the spouse, the closest non-family friend (Ray), and the mentee (Marcus). Pastor Dale and Walt are notable omissions but cannot be added without dropping a family member or Ray; the current allocation is defensible on family-priority grounds.
